description: Imports Google Analytics GA4 property reports (users, devices, locations, pages, traffic sources, plus user-defined custom reports) as daily dimension/metric rows via the Analytics Data API runReport endpoint.

spec.apiVersionPinning: path segment (`/v1beta/`) in the hardcoded base URL

credentialModes.name: Google OAuth 2.0 (client id + secret + refresh token)

configFields.name: property_id
configFields.description: GA4 property identifier whose events are tracked; interpolated into the runReport path.

configFields.name: custom_reports
configFields.description: A JSON array (supplied as a string) of custom report definitions; each entry becomes an additional binding. Default empty.

configFields.name: start_date
configFields.description: UTC datetime; earliest data replicated. Defaults to 30 days ago; must be >= 2015-08-14T00:00:00Z and <= now.

configFields.name: credentials.credentials_title
configFields.description: Discriminator; the only value is "OAuth Credentials".

configFields.name: advanced.lookback_window_size
configFields.description: Days to look back from the incremental cursor for late-arriving report updates. Default 30, min 0.

configFields.name: interval
configFields.description: ISO-8601 duration between updates for this binding; discovery recommends PT12H.

paginator.notes: limit/offset are JSON request-body fields of the runReport POST, not query params. offset advances by 250000 each iteration; loop ends when the response body's rowCount is absent or offset >= rowCount.

backfill.notes: One calendar day per page cursor: body dateRanges[0].startDate == endDate == the cursor day; the page cursor is an ISO datetime string advanced by one day and stops at the backfill cutoff.

streams.notes: Archetype, not a real stream. Each object in the endpoint-config `custom_reports` JSON array becomes one additional binding with the same pull shape as the eight shipped reports. Fields: name, dimensions (1-9), metrics (1-10), optional dimensionFilter, metricFilter, metricAggregations (TOTAL|MINIMUM|MAXIMUM). Names colliding with a default report are rejected at validation.

authTierRationale: The endpoint config offers exactly one credentials variant: BaseOAuth2Credentials specialized for provider "google", requiring client_id, client_secret and refresh_token, all three marked required and secret in the spec snapshot. There is no API-key / access-token / service-account alternative in this connector, even though the shared CDK supports GoogleServiceAccount and AccessToken (the connector imports AccessToken but never uses it in EndpointConfig). Standalone, a user must register their own Google Cloud OAuth client AND complete the consent flow to obtain a refresh token, hence T3. Estuary's hosted control plane can hide this: the spec ships an oauth2 block (authUrlTemplate/accessTokenUrlTemplate/accessTokenResponseMap extracting /refresh_token) so the platform performs the authorization_code exchange with its own registered app and injects the three fields. That platform assistance does not change the standalone tier.

unionMisfits.description: Pagination is offset/limit by semantics but body-expressed by transport: `limit` and `offset` are JSON fields of the runReport POST body, not query parameters. The `offset` paginator variant has no place to say WHERE the values are sent (no tokenTo), while `body_cursor` implies an opaque token and cannot express a numeric offset plus a page size. Chose `offset` (semantics win, since the value is a plain integer row offset) and added a non-schema `tokenTo: body_field` plus a note.

The incremental bound is not a request parameter at all: the connector sends dateRanges[{startDate, endDate}] in the POST body with both set to a single calendar day, and iterates one day per request. incrementalParam assumes a single named param carrying a timestamp, so it is null here even though the connector is very much incremental.

There is a third pull leg the union cannot hold: before paginating each day, the connector issues an extra runReport with limit=1, offset=0 purely to read dimensionHeaders/metricHeaders, which are then used to name the columns of every row. It is a per-day schema probe, neither backfill, incremental, nor snapshot.

After the last page of a day, the connector emits up to three extra documents built from the response's totals/minimums/maximums arrays, using the same document model and the same key as ordinary rows. These aggregate rows are a different record semantics sharing one stream; the schema has no way to mark a stream as emitting mixed row kinds.

The stream list is neither purely static nor `discovered` in the schema's sense. Eight reports are hardcoded; additional bindings come from a user-authored JSON array in the endpoint config, validated against dimension/metric names fetched from the property's /metadata endpoint. That is user-configured, not schema-discovered, so `discovery` is null and streamMode is `static` with an archetype entry.

abstained.transports[0].spec.defaultHeaders: No static default headers are set on the session; the only header the connector contributes is Authorization: Bearer <token>, added by the CDK TokenSource, and Content-Type from the JSON body helper. Nothing connector-specific to report.
abstained.execution.defaultSchedule: No connector-wide schedule exists. The only schedule is the per-binding ResourceConfig interval (12h) set at discovery, which the user may override; recorded on each stream instead.
abstained.streams[*].pull.*.incrementalParam: Not applicable — the date bound travels in the POST body's dateRanges, not in a named parameter. See unionMisfits.
abstained.streams[*].pull.*.params: The runReport call takes no query parameters; everything (dimensions, metrics, dateRanges, limit, offset, filters, aggregations) is in the JSON body.
abstained.discovery: There is no schema discovery. The eight reports are hardcoded and any extra bindings come from a user-written JSON array in endpoint config; the /metadata call is used only to validate dimension/metric names, never to enumerate streams.
abstained.streams[*].writeDisposition: Inferred, not stated. The key includes property_id + report_date + all dimensions and the lookback window deliberately re-emits the same days, so re-captured documents overwrite by key (merge). The connector never emits deletes or tombstones, and _meta.op defaults to 'u'.
abstained.streams[*].cursorField: The engine-level cursor is a Python datetime LogCursor held in connector state, not a document field. 'report_date' is the document field it corresponds to; treat the mapping as inferred.
